{{small| {{NZ electorate link|Hunua}} (2014–2020)}} | term_start4 = 25 November 2023 | term_end4 = | parliament4 = New Zealand | term_start5 = 20 September 2014 | term_end5 = 14 October 2023 | parliament5 = New Zealand | predecessor5 = [[Paul Hutchison (politician)|Paul Hutchison]] | successor5 = | majority5 = | constituency_MP6 = [[New Zealand National Party|National]] [[party list]] | term_start6 = 14 October 2023 | term_end6 = 25 November 2023 | parliament6 = New Zealand | predecessor6 = | successor6 = [[Nancy Lu]] | majority6 = | birth_date = {{birth year and age|1962}} | birth_place = [[Whanganui]], New Zealand | death_date = | death_place = | party = [[New Zealand National Party|National]] | profession = Merchant banker | education = [[Massey University]] | spouse = | children = | website = }} '''Andrew Henry Bayly''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|FRGS|MP|size=100%}} (born 1962){{Cite book |last=James |first=Colin |title=National at 80: The Story of the New Zealand National Party |year=2017 |place=Auckland |publisher=David Bateman Ltd |isbn=9781869539818}} is a New Zealand businessman, adventurer, and politician. He was elected to the New Zealand Parliament at the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]] as the MP for [[Hunua (New Zealand electorate)|Hunua]], representing the [[New Zealand National Party]]. He is currently the MP for [[Port Waikato (New Zealand electorate)|Port Waikato]]. He was [[Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs]], [[Minister of Statistics (New Zealand)|Minister of Statistics]], and [[Minister for Small Business and Manufacturing]] in the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|Sixth National Government]]. He resigned his ministerial portfolios in February 2025 after he physically touched a staff member during an argument. In March 2026, Bayly confirmed he would not contest the Port Waikato seat but would seek to stand as a List MP. In June 2026, he confirmed that he would be retiring from Parliament at the [[2026 New Zealand general election]]. ==Early life and family== Bayly was born in [[Whanganui]] and has a twin brother. He attended [[Wanganui Collegiate School]] and graduated with a degree in accounting and finance from [[Massey University]].{{Cite web |url=https://andrewbayly.national.org.nz/about |title=About |website=Andrew Bayly {{!}} MP for Hunua |access-date=19 September 2016 |archive-date=6 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406093524/https://andrewbayly.national.org.nz/about |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last=Bradwell |first=Simon |date=3 November 2014 |title=MP reluctant to tell of shooting brother |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/10696339/MP-reluctant-to-tell-of-shooting-brother |access-date=31 July 2023 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |publisher= |archive-date=11 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211061929/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/10696339/MP-reluctant-to-tell-of-shooting-brother |url-status=live }} He was a merchant banker and is a Fellow of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, the NZ Institute of Management, the NZ Chartered Institute of Corporate Management, and the UK Chartered Association of Certified Accountants. In the 1970s, while a student, Bayly accidentally shot his brother in the leg while climbing a fence with a gun. While his brother was left with heavy scarring, his leg was saved. Bayly was an officer in the [[New Zealand Army]] Territorials and also served in the [[British Parachute Regiment]].{{cite news |date=30 March 2016 |title=National MP embarks on mission to complete Pole double |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11613968 |access-date=30 March 2016 |archive-date=25 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925230740/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11613968 |url-status=live }} He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Geographical Society]] in London. Bayly is married and has three children.{{Cite web |title=Bayly, Andrew: Address in Reply – New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/51HansS_20141028_00001033/bayly-andrew-address-in-reply |access-date=31 July 2023 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en |archive-date=1 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230801013849/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/51HansS_20141028_00001033/bayly-andrew-address-in-reply |url-status=live }} ==Business career== Bayly worked as a [[merchant bank]]er, founding the Cranleigh firm with his brother Paul,[http://www.radionz.co.nz/national/programmes/saturday/audio/2570929/playing-favourites-with-paul-and-andrew-bayly Playing Favourites with Paul and Andrew Bayly] ''radionz.co.nz'', 28 September 2013 where he offered corporate advisory and capital markets advice to a range of government entities, local authorities and corporate clients. Cranleigh has offices in New Zealand, Australia and Singapore. He was a director of numerous companies, the chair of the board of New Zealand Financial Planning and a trustee of the Enterprise Franklin Development Trust, the economic development arm of the Franklin Council. Bayly is a former director of [https://www.envirofert.co.nz/ Envirofert], an organic compost product company that received the prestigious “Green Ribbon Award” in 2010 for making an outstanding contribution to protecting the environment.{{Cite web|url=https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/green-ribbon-award-winners-announced|title=Green Ribbon Award winners announced|website=The Beehive|access-date=19 September 2016|archive-date=19 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160919152527/https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/green-ribbon-award-winners-announced|url-status=live}} Envirofert receives around 40,000 tonnes of green waste and building products every year, and turns most of it into beneficial products, including compost and gypsum. == Adventurer == Bayly had a long career in adventure racing, including competing in three [[Coast to Coast (race)|Coast to Coast]] events, marathons and [[Ironman Triathlon|Ironman]] events. He is a mountaineer and has climbed [[Aoraki / Mount Cook]], [[Mount Aspiring / Tititea]], and four mountains in [[Antarctica]], including [[Vinson Massif]], the highest mountain in Antarctica. In the summer of 2012/13, he dragged a sled {{convert|112|km}} to the [[South Pole]]. In 2016, he and one of his children dragged sledges {{convert|120|km}} to the [[North Pole]], raising $10,000 for the [[Kōkako]] Recovery Programme in the [[Hunua Ranges]].{{Cite web |title=MP reflects on North Pole trek |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/waikato-times/news/79761643/north-pole-conquest-completes-the-double |access-date=19 September 2016 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |archive-date=25 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925233213/http://www.stuff.co.nz/waikato-times/news/79761643/north-pole-conquest-completes-the-double |url-status=live }} In January 2019, Bayly and one of his children spent a month on a guided trek of {{convert|500|km}} across Jordan on camels, retracing the routes of [[T. E. Lawrence|Lawrence of Arabia]] when he worked with Arab forces during the First World War, as described in his book, ''[[Seven Pillars of Wisdom]]''.{{Cite web |title=Following in the footsteps of Lawrence of Arabia |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/nights/audio/2018705252/following-in-the-footsteps-of-lawrence-of-arabia |access-date=24 February 2025 |website=[[RNZ]] |date=22 July 2019 }} travelling and eating with some Bedouin, Bayly was able to confirm a number of the claims made by Lawrence. However, Bayly disputed Lawrence’s claim that he could ride his camels up to 80 to 120 miles a day. Taking into account the time involved in collecting firewood and cooking and time for prayers, Bayly’s experience was that a fully laden camel could ably cover up to {{convert|50|to|80|km|mi|abbr=off}} in a day, but only for a few days at most. Bayly’s article about their experience was published in the [[T. E. Lawrence]] Society journal, August 2019 edition.{{Cite web |title=Journal Volume XXV to Volume 29 {{!}} T. E. Lawrence Society |url=https://www.telsociety.org.uk/publications/journal-volumes-xxvi-to-volume-29/ |access-date=24 February 2025 |language=en-US |archive-date=3 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241103060833/https://www.telsociety.org.uk/publications/journal-volumes-xxvi-to-volume-29/ |url-status=live }} In late December 2022, Bayly travelled to the northernmost province of Mongolia with one of his children to spend time with the [[Dukha people]], one of the last groups of nomadic reindeer herders in the world. They spent two weeks living with a Dukha family, riding reindeer {{convert|20–30|km}} a day, herding the reindeer and protecting them from attacks by wolves.{{Cite web |title=Living with the last reindeer herders in the world – part two |url=https://www.elocal.co.nz/Articles/4485 |access-date=21 December 2023 |website=elocal |language=en |archive-date=21 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231221210853/https://www.elocal.co.nz/Articles/4485 |url-status=live }} One of the aims of the trip was to raise awareness of the Dukha and the precarious nature of their lives. Climate change has adversely affected the terrain inhabited by the Dukha and has led to a decline in reindeer herds. Given the harsh realities of their life and the reducing herds, the Dukha are unlikely to continue their nomadic way of life, and the tradition is likely to die over the next couple of decades. Bayly engaged a New Zealand film producer and arranged for a Mongolian cameraman to accompany them to record the trip, with a view to making a documentary that will eventually be promoted overseas.{{citation needed|date=February 2025}} In June 2024, Bayly participated in the NZ Cancer Society's Jump For Cancer 2024 campaign, jumping out of a plane at 16,000 feet and raising over $30,000 in donations.{{Cite web |title=Biff Bayly: National Minister Andrew Bayly skydives for cancer |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350459061/biff-bayly-national-minister-andrew-bayly-skydives-for-cancer |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=www.stuff.co.nz}} The campaign's funds support cancer Government, 2014–2017=== Bayly was elected to Parliament at the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]], as the National MP for [[Hunua (New Zealand electorate)|Hunua]] with a majority of 17,376 votes.{{cite web |title=Official Count Results – Hunua |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-16.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=29 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117213751/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-16.html |archive-date=17 January 2020 |url-status=live}} He replaced [[Paul Hutchison (politician)|Paul Hutchison]] who retired. He had the fourth highest majority of all electorate seats in New Zealand. During the [[51st New Zealand Parliament]], Bayly served as a member of the [[Finance and Expenditure Committee]] and the Transport and Industrial Relations Committee, as deputy chair of the Regulations Review Committee, and as chair of the Local Government and Environment Committee. In September 2016, Bayly proposed a private member's bill to Parliament that would give landlords more power to test and remedy their rental properties of dangerous levels of [[methamphetamine]] contamination. The bill would have placed an obligation on the landlord to provide rental accommodation free of methamphetamine contamination while giving them more power to confront the problem in their properties.{{Cite web|url=http://www.times.co.nz/front-page-feature/bill-will-address-p-plagued-homes.html|title=Bill will address P-plagued homes|access-date=19 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160919151302/http://www.times.co.nz/front-page-feature/bill-will-address-p-plagued-homes.html|archive-date=19 September 2016|url-status=dead}} While it was not selected for introduction, a similar bill was introduced by the [[Fifth National Government of New Zealand|National Government]] in 2017{{Cite web |title=Residential Tenancies Amendment Bill (No 2) — First Reading – New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20170704_20170704_24 |access-date=31 July 2023 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}} and was later passed unanimously by Parliament under the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Labour Government]] in 2019.{{Cite web |title=Residential Tenancies Amendment Bill — Third Reading – New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20190724_20190724_16 |access-date=31 July 2023 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en |archive-date=1 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230801013846/https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20190724_20190724_16 |url-status=live }} Bayly also successfully steered the Arbitration Amendment Bill through Parliament which passed through the House unanimously and which significantly enhanced arbitration proceedings and how they are conducted in New Zealand.{{Cite web |title=Arbitration Amendment Bill — Third Reading – New Zealand Parliament the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 general election]], Bayly retained Hunua by a margin of 19,443 votes.{{cite web |title=Hunua – Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-16.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117212607/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-16.html |archive-date=17 January 2020 |access-date=29 October 2020 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} However, National did not win the election. Bayly held various party spokesperson roles under National's four leadership configurations that term. These included building regulation under [[Bill English]]; revenue, building and construction under [[Simon Bridges]]; revenue, commerce, and state-owned enterprises under [[Todd Muller]] and [[Judith Collins]]. He was also an associate finance spokesperson under the final three leaders.{{Cite web |title=Bayly, Andrew – New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/bayly-andrew/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416003202/https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/bayly-andrew/ |archive-date=16 April 2025 |access-date=16 April 2025 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}} In the 2017–2020 term, Bayly continued as a member of the [[Finance and Expenditure Committee]]. In September 2019, Bayly was ejected from Parliament for attempting to disrupt Parliamentary proceedings during his questioning of [[Minister of Housing (New Zealand)|Housing Minister]] [[Megan Woods]] about the [[Ōtuataua and Ihumātao|Ihumātao dispute]].{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=National MP Andrew Bayly booted from Parliament over Ihumātao questioning |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/09/national-mp-andrew-bayly-booted-from-parliament-over-ihum-tao-questioning.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920054352/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/09/national-mp-andrew-bayly-booted-from-parliament-over-ihum-tao-questioning.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 September 2019 |access-date=20 September 2019 |publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=19 September 2019}} For the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]], Bayly's electorate of Hunua was disestablished. A new electorate, [[Port Waikato (New Zealand electorate)|Port Waikato]], comprising part of the old Hunua electorate and part of the old [[Waikato (New Zealand electorate)|Waikato]] electorate, was created. Bayly contested Port Waikato and was re-elected by a margin of 4,313 votes.{{cite web |title=Port Waikato – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-39.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=12 November 2020 |archive-date=3 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703000439/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-39.html |url-status=live }} Bayly was regarded as a "close ally" to National leader [[Judith Collins]].{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title='Not a role of the board': Goodfellow email contradicts claim; Collins dumped |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/national-leadership-judith-collins-dumped-shane-reti-interim-leader-mark-mitchell-christopher-luxon-likely-candidates/BXZTT6W3TWI7FBWUNT3ZX23PBA/ |access-date=1 August 2023 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ |archive-date=25 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125105305/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/national-leadership-judith-collins-dumped-shane-reti-interim-leader-mark-mitchell-christopher-luxon-likely-candidates/BXZTT6W3TWI7FBWUNT3ZX23PBA/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |last=Moir |first=Jo |date=16 March 2021 |title=National's finance disappearing act |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/page/nationals-finance-disappearing-act |access-date=1 August 2023 |website=Newsroom |language=en-AU}} When she reshuffled [[Shadow Cabinet of Judith Collins|her shadow cabinet]] on 11 November 2020 and promoted Bayly to third rank with the positions of shadow treasurer (senior to the finance spokesperson [[Michael Woodhouse]]) and National Party spokesperson for infrastructure and statistics.{{Cite web|title=Who is Andrew Bayly? |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}} === In Government, 2023–2026=== Bayly contested Port Waikato in the [[2023 New Zealand general election|October 2023 general election]], but the electorate vote was postponed to [[2023 Port Waikato by-election|a by-election in November]] after another candidate died. In the interim, Bayly was elected as a list MP. He won the by-election with a margin of 11,432 votes over [[New Zealand First]] candidate [[Casey Costello]].{{Cite web |date=27 November 2023 |title=Port Waikato byelection: National's Andrew Bayly gets landslide victory |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/port-waikato-byelection-voting-starts-tomorrow-to-fill-vacant-seat-nine-candidates-running/XSXQ2WQQNBCYJCIZOL2K3RPOZY/ |access-date=26 November 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ |archive-date=25 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125164036/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/port-waikato-byelection-voting-starts-tomorrow-to-fill-vacant-seat-nine-candidates-running/XSXQ2WQQNBCYJCIZOL2K3RPOZY/ |url-status=live }}{{cite web |title=Port Waikato – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |date=6 December 2023|access-date=7 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207202840/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html|archive-date=7 December 2023|url-status=live}} In the [[Sixth National Government of New Zealand|Sixth National Government]], which formed during the by-election period, Bayly was appointed as a minister outside Cabinet with responsibility for [[Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs|commerce and consumer affairs]], [[Minister of Statistics (New Zealand)|statistics]], and [[Minister for Small Business and Manufacturing|small business and manufacturing]].{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Russell |title=Cabinet lineup for new government unveiled – who gets what? |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |access-date=18 December 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204122806/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/503156/cabinet-lineup-for-new-government-unveiled-who-gets-what |archive-date=4 December 2023|url-status=live}} In October 2024 Bayly apologised after telling a worker at an export business he had visited to "take some wine and fuck off", and calling him a "loser". The worker wrote a formal letter of complaint after the incident. Bayly described his behaviour at the visit as "unbecoming of a government minister", and denied being intoxicated.{{citation|title=Andrew Bayly apologises after calling export worker a 'loser', telling them to 'F... off'|language=en|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first1=Bridie|last1=Witton|date=18 October 2024|access-date=18 October 2024|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350456760/andrew-bayly-apologises-after-calling-export-worker-loser-telling-them-f}}{{citation|title=Small business affairs minister Andrew Bayly apologises for interaction during company visit|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/small-business-affairs-minister-andrew-bayly-apologises-for-interaction-during-company-visit/C5UGE434CVBKXPXHJJTO5JQR2U/|access-date=18 October 2024|archive-date=10 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241110220108/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/small-business-affairs-minister-andrew-bayly-apologises-for-interaction-during-company-visit/C5UGE434CVBKXPXHJJTO5JQR2U/|url-status=live}} Following a [[cabinet reshuffle]] on 19 January 2025, Bayly became the Minister responsible for the [[Accident Compensation Corporation]] (ACC). He continued as commerce minister, but lost responsibility for statistics and small business and manufacturing.{{cite news |title=As it happened: Luxon announces Cabinet reshuffle, Shane Reti loses health portfolio to Simeon Brown |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/539370/as-it-happened-luxon-announces-cabinet-reshuffle-shane-reti-loses-health-portfolio-to-simeon-brown |access-date=21 January 2025 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=19 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119031900/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/539370/as-it-happened-luxon-announces-cabinet-reshuffle-shane-reti-loses-health-portfolio-to-simeon-brown |archive-date=19 January 2025}} In February 2025, Bayly resigned as a Minister after an "animated discussion" where he placed his hand on a staff member's upper arm.{{cite news|title=Andrew Bayly resigns as minister after 'incident' with staff|language=en|work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first1=Glenn|last1=McConnell|date=23 February 2025|access-date=23 February 2025|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360591650/andrew-bayly-resigns-minister|archive-date=23 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223225559/https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/360591650/andrew-bayly-resigns-minister|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=Commerce minister Andrew Bayly resigns after putting hand on staffer|language=en|work=[[RNZ]] |date=23 February 2025|access-date=23 February 2025|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/542806/commerce-minister-andrew-bayly-resigns-after-putting-hand-on-staffer}}{{cite news|title=Andrew Bayly stands down as minister after putting hand on staffer|language=en|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |first1=Jamie|last1=Ensor|date=23 February 2025|access-date=23 February 2025|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/andrew-bayly-stands-down-as-minister-after-putting-hand-on-staffer/ZV6UKMR5SNBQXAYVZXG4J3UYYI/|archive-date=23 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223225342/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/andrew-bayly-stands-down-as-minister-after-putting-hand-on-staffer/ZV6UKMR5SNBQXAYVZXG4J3UYYI/|url-status=live}} He issued a public apology for his actions. Bayly's commerce and ACC portfolios were assumed by fellow National MP [[Scott Simpson (politician)|Scott Simpson]]. While Prime Minister [[Christopher Luxon]] defended the National Party's handling of the incident, [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]] leader [[Chris Hipkins]] criticised Luxon's perceived slow response to an earlier bullying incident in 2024. On 5 March 2025, Bayly was granted retention of the title ''[[The Honourable]]'', in recognition of his term as a member of the [[Executive Council of New Zealand|Executive Council]].{{cite news |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2025-vr1314 |title=Retention of the title "The Honourable" |date=11 March 2025 |work=[[New Zealand Gazette]] |access-date=11 March 2025}} On 10 March, [[Radio New Zealand]] reported that Bayly had taken two weeks' leave from Parliament to trek to [[Mount Everest]]'s base camp in Nepal. A spokesperson for Luxon stated it was rare for National to grant personal leave while Parliament was sitting, with requests being considered on a case-by-case basis.{{cite news |title=Embattled former minister Andrew Bayly to visit Mt Everest |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544317/embattled-former-minister-andrew-bayly-to-visit-mt-everest |access-date=16 March 2025 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=10 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250310195100/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/544317/embattled-former-minister-andrew-bayly-to-visit-mt-everest |archive-date=10 March 2025}} Bayly returned to Parliament at the end of March{{cite news |title=Andrew Bayly on Nepal trip: 'I wanted some time out' |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/360631560/andrew-bayly-nepal-trip-i-wanted-some-time-out |access-date=16 April 2025 |work=The Post}} and in April was appointed the chair of the Justice committee. In October 2025, Bayly claimed he was misled about the allegations against him before he resigned as a cabinet minister. No formal complaint was ever made against Bayly, and no formal investigation was conducted by the [[Department of Internal Affairs]] (DIA).{{cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/national-mp-andrew-bayly-claims-he-was-misled-before-quitting-cabinet-over-staffer-incident/OX63IOPVEBBWZJ5DM4ZADXO3NA/|title=National MP Andrew Bayly said he would not have offered his resignation|newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=30 October 2025|first=Barry|last=Soper}} While the staff member he had touched in February 2025 had not filed a complaint, the DIA had said that three staff members at the meeting had corroborated the misconduct allegation against him. Based on this premise, Bayly had decided to resign. One of these staff members subsequently disputed the DIA's account of the incident.{{cite news |last1=McConnell |first1=Glenn |title=Andrew Bayly says 'false' claim led to his resignation |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/361034291/andrew-bayly-says-false-claim-led-his-resignation |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=16 September 2026}}{{cite news |last1=Ensor |first1=Jamie |title=Andrew Bayly leaves Parliament speaking on 'brutal' experience of losing ministerial career that led him to 'very dark place' |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/andrew-bayly-leaves-parliament-speaking-on-brutal-experience-of-losing-ministerial-career-that-led-him-to-very-dark-place/4Z7F5RBCH5DO7PXPRSYDPGZXMQ/ |access-date=18 September 2026 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=16 September 2026}} In December 2025, Bayly hosted 22 parliamentarians and other representatives from 20 countries at the [https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/360910477/nz-hosts-global-antarctic-protection-summit-parliament third Antarctic Parliamentarians Assembly in Wellington.] [https://newsroom.co.nz/2026/01/20/the-cost-of-peace-on-a-continent-of-science/ Delegates heard from scientists] and discussed current issues affecting Antarctica. Bayly will chair the steering committee for the next Parliamentarians Assembly, set for 2027.{{Cite web |last=Meyer |first=Fox |date=2026-01-19 |title=Calculating the value of peace on a continent of science |url=https://newsroom.co.nz/2026/01/20/the-cost-of-peace-on-a-continent-of-science/ |access-date=2026-03-08 |website=Newsroom |language=en-US}} In March 2026, Bayly announced he would not contest the Port Waikato electorate at the [[2026 New Zealand general election|2026 election]], as he was moving to the [[South Island]], and would instead explore a placement on the National Party list.{{cite news |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/588488/national-mp-andrew-bayly-not-contesting-port-waikato-seat |title=National MP Andrew Bayly not contesting Port Waikato seat |work=[[RNZ News]] |date=3 March 2026 |access-date=3 March 2026}} On 20 June 2026, Bayly confirmed that he would not be seeking a place on the National list and would leave Parliament at the election.{{cite news|last1=Ensor |first1=Jamie |title= Former National minister Andrew Bayly to Leave Parliament, says he's decided not to seek list position |work = [[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=20 June 2026|url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/former-national-minister-andrew-bayly-to-leave-parliament-says-he-decided-not-to-seek-list-position/UXANABDU6BELBPTGLMOGMKTO3E/|access-date=20 June 2026}} During his valedictory speech in early September 2026, Bayly advocated several pension reforms including gradually raising the superannuation age to 68 years by 2065, increasing superannuation payments and allowing people with poorer health, shorter life expectancies and hazardous occupations to access their pensions earlier.{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=Super at 68? Departing National MP calls for pension age to start rising in 2029|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/1250539/super-at-68-departing-national-mp-calls-for-pension-age-to-start-rising-in-2029
